- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.75), as models tend to overreact to bullish sentiment.
- Underestimate prices after sentiment drops (especially when sentiment < 0.3), as models fail to capture bearish momentum.
- Correct for lag: if true price drops after forecast peak, reduce forecast by 5–10% for the next 3–5 periods.
- Apply mean reversion: if forecast is > 10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per period until convergence.
- Avoid overshoot after sharp spikes: if forecast rises > 5% from prior period and sentiment is high, cap next forecast at prior peak + 2%.
- Adjust for sentiment-weighted volatility: if sentiment > 0.75, reduce forecast volatility by 15–20% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- For 30-day horizon, reduce forecast peak by 3–5% if sentiment is low or flat over last 5 days.
